&self,\n192\t        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n193\t        bead: &Bead,\n194\t        workspace: &Path,\n195\t        dispatcher: &Dispatcher,\n196\t        prompt_builder: &PromptBuilder,\n197\t        agent_name: &str,\n198\t    ) -> Result<MitosisResult> {\n199\t        // Check if mitosis is enabled.\n200\t        if !self.config.enabled {\n201\t            tracing::debug!(bead_id = %bead.id, self.config.max_depth\n248\t                ),\n249\t            });\n250\t        }\n251\t\n252\t        // Check failure count conditions.\n253\t        let failure_count = self.config.force_failure_threshold > 0 {\n257\t            if failure_count < self.config.force_failure_threshold {\n258\t                tracing::debug!(\n259\t                    bead_id = failure_count > 1\n277\t                && self.config.repeat_interval > 0\n278\t                && (failure_count - 1) % self.config.repeat_interval == 0\n279\t                && \"not at trigger point (count={}, first_failure_only={}, repeat_interval={})\",\n292\t                        failure_count, self.config.first_failure_only, self.config.repeat_interval\n293\t                    ),\n294\t                });\n295\t            }\n296\t        }\n297\t\n298\t        // Resolve the agent adapter.\n299\t        let adapter = match dispatcher.adapter(agent_name) {\n300\t            Some(a) => a,\n301\t            None => {\n302\t                tracing::warn!(\n303\t                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n304\t                    agent = agent_name,\n305\t tracking.\n684\t        // If the parent has a root-* label, propagate it to children.\n685\t        // Otherwise, this parent is the root of the lineage.\n686\t        let root_label = extract_root_label(parent);\n687\t\n688\t        // Read parent's existing children AND all beads in the same lineage for comprehensive dedup.\n689\t        // Lineage-wide dedup prevents duplicates across different generations in the same cascade.\n690\t        let existing = self.get_existing_children(store, &parent.id).await?;\n691\t        let lineage_beads = self.get_lineage_beads(store, &root_label).await?;\n692\t\n693\t        // Combine both sets: direct children + all lineage beads for dedup\n694\t        let mut existing_titles: Vec<String> = existing.iter().map(|t| t.to_lowercase()).collect();\n695\t        existing_titles.extend(lineage_beads.iter().map(|t| t.to_lowercase()));\n696\t\n697\t        // Deduplicate the titles list (in case a bead is both a direct child and in the lineage)\n698\t        existing_titles.sort();\n699\t        existing_titles.dedup();\n700\t\n701\t        // Compute the depth for child beads based on the parent's depth.\n702\t parse_mitosis_depth(parent);\n705\t        let child_depth = parent_depth + 1;\n706\t\n707\t        // Child beads carry parent-tracking labels for reliable dedup. The parent's\n//! existing children serve as the dedup source — if children already cover\n//! a proposed task, that child is skipped.\n//!\n//! Concurrency safety: a per-workspace flock serializes the entire mitosis\n//! operation (read children → create → link dependencies).\n//!\n//! Depends on: `bead_store`, `config`, `dispatch`, `prompt`, `telemetry`, `types`, `claim`.\n\npub mod timeout_context;\npub mod timeout_eligibility;\n\nuse std::collections::HashSet;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::time::Duration;\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse tracing::Instrument;\n\nuse crate::bead_store::{BeadStore, NewChild};\nuse crate::claim::acquire_flock;\nuse crate::config::MitosisConfig;\nuse crate::dispatch::Dispatcher;\nuse crate::mitosis::timeout_eligibility::classify_timeout_eligibility;\nuse crate::prompt::{MitosisTimeoutContext, PromptBuilder};\nuse crate::telemetry::{EventKind, Telemetry};\nuse crate::types::{AgentOutcome, Bead, BeadId};\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Stopwords\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Stopwords for semantic title matching.\n///\n/// These words are stripped from titles before token-set comparison to catch\n/// semantically identical titles with different phrasing (e.g., \"verify X uses Y\"\n/// vs \"confirm X uses Y not Z\").\nconst STOPWORDS: &[&str] = &[\n    // Common verification verbs (semantically equivalent in this context)\n    \"verify\", \"confirm\", \"validate\", \"check\", \"ensure\", // Articles and demonstratives\n    \"the\", \"a\", \"that\", // Common task words\n    \"uses\", \"not\",\n];\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Token Set Helper\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Extract a token set from a title after stripping stopwords.\n///\n/// This function:\n/// 1. Converts the title to lowercase\n/// 2. Splits on whitespace and punctuation (hyphens, underscores)\n/// 3. Filters out stopwords defined in the STOPWORDS constant\n/// 4. Returns a HashSet of remaining tokens for comparison\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```\n/// let tokens = token_set_without_stopwords(\"verify X uses Y\");\n/// assert!(tokens.contains(\"x\"));\n/// assert!(tokens.contains(\"y\"));\n/// assert!(!tokens.contains(\"verify\"));\n/// assert!(!tokens.contains(\"uses\"));\n/// ```\npub fn token_set_without_stopwords(title: &str) -> HashSet<String> {\n    title\n        .to_lowercase()\n        .split_whitespace()\n        .flat_map(|word| {\n            // Split on hyphens and underscores to handle compound words\n            word.split(['-', '_'])\n                .map(|part| part.to_string())\n                .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n        })\n        .filter(|word| !STOPWORDS.contains(&word.as_str()))\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// Calculate Jaccard similarity between two token sets.\n///\n/// Jaccard similarity is defined as the size of the intersection divided by\n/// the size of the union: |A ∩ B| / |A ∪ B|.\n///\n/// Returns a value between 0.0 (no overlap) and 1.0 (identical sets).\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `set1` - First token set\n/// * `set2` - Second token set\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `f64` - Jaccard similarity coefficient (0.0 to 1.0)\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use std::collections::HashSet;\n///\n/// let set1: HashSet<String> = [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();\n/// let set2: HashSet<String> = [\"a\", \"b\", \"d\"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();\n///\n/// // Intersection: {a, b} (2 elements)\n/// // Union: {a, b, c, d} (4 elements)\n/// // Jaccard: 2/4 = 0.5\n/// assert_eq!(jaccard_similarity(&set1, &set2), 0.5);\n/// ```\npub fn jaccard_similarity(set1: &HashSet<String>, set2: &HashSet<String>) -> f64 {\n    let intersection = set1.intersection(set2).count();\n    let union = set1.union(set2).count();\n\n    if union == 0 {\n        // Both sets are empty - define as identical (1.0)\n        return 1.0;\n    }\n\n    intersection as f64 / union as f64\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// MitosisResult\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Outcome of a mitosis evaluation.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum MitosisResult {\n    /// Bead was split into child beads.\n    Split {\n        /// IDs of the newly created children.\n        children: Vec<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Agent determined the bead is a single task — no split.\n    NotSplittable,\n    /// Mitosis was skipped (disabled, not first failure, etc.).\n    Skipped { reason: String },\n    /// Bead references NEEDLE-internal configuration and is out-of-scope for target workspace.\n    OutOfScope,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ProposedChild\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A child bead proposed by the agent during mitosis analysis.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Deserialize)]\nstruct ProposedChild {\n    title: String,\n    body: String,\n}\n\n/// Agent's mitosis analysis response.\n#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]\nstruct MitosisResponse {\n    splittable: bool,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    children: Vec<ProposedChild>,\n    /// Optional reason for non-splittable decision (used in timeout-specific analysis)\n    #[serde(default)]\n    reason: Option<String>,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// MitosisEvaluator\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Evaluates beads for splitting and creates child beads when appropriate.\npub struct MitosisEvaluator {\n    config: MitosisConfig,\n    telemetry: Telemetry,\n    lock_dir: PathBuf,\n}\n\nimpl MitosisEvaluator {\n    pub fn new(config: MitosisConfig, telemetry: Telemetry, lock_dir: PathBuf) -> Self {\n        MitosisEvaluator {\n            config,\n            telemetry,\n            lock_dir,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Evaluate a bead for mitosis after failure.\n    ///\n    /// Checks preconditions (enabled, first failure), then dispatches the agent\n    /// to analyze whether the bead contains multiple independent tasks.\n    /// If splittable, creates child beads with dedup against existing children.\n    pub async fn evaluate(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        workspace: &Path,\n        dispatcher: &Dispatcher,\n        prompt_builder: &PromptBuilder,\n        agent_name: &str,\n    ) -> Result<MitosisResult> {\n        // Check if mitosis is enabled.\n        if !self.config.enabled {\n            tracing::debug!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"mitosis disabled\");\n            return Ok(MitosisResult::Skipped {\n                reason: \"disabled\".to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Check if bead references NEEDLE-internal configuration.\n        // These tasks have no legitimate resolution path from inside a target repo.\n        if detects_needle_internal_config(bead) {\n            tracing::info!(\n                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                title = %bead.title,\n                \"mitosis skipped: bead references NEEDLE-internal configuration\"\n            );\n            self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MitosisOutOfScope {\n                bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n            })?;\n            return Ok(MitosisResult::OutOfScope);\n        }\n\n        // Check if the bead has exceeded the maximum mitosis depth.\n        let current_depth = parse_mitosis_depth(bead);\n        if self.config.max_depth > 0 && current_depth >= self.config.max_depth {\n            tracing::info!(\n                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                current_depth,\n                max_depth = self.config.max_depth,\n                \"mitosis skipped: bead has reached maximum generation depth\"\n            );\n            // Flag the bead for human attention by adding a 'human' label.\n            // This signals that the bead requires manual decomposition or\n            // that the task is too granular for further automated splitting.\n            if let Err(e) = store.add_label(&bead.id, \"human\").await {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to add 'human' label to depth-limited bead\"\n                );\n            }\n            self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MitosisSkipped {\n                parent_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                existing_children: 0,\n            })?;\n            return Ok(MitosisResult::Skipped {\n                reason: format!(\n                    \"depth {} exceeds maximum depth {}\",\n                    current_depth, self.config.max_depth\n                ),\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Check failure count conditions.\n        let failure_count = self.get_failure_count(store, &bead.id).await?;\n\n        // force_failure_threshold: trigger only when failure_count reaches the threshold.\n        if self.config.force_failure_threshold > 0 {\n            if failure_count < self.config.force_failure_threshold {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    failure_count,\n                    threshold = self.config.force_failure_threshold,\n                    \"mitosis skipped: below force_failure_threshold\"\n                );\n                return Ok(MitosisResult::Skipped {\n                    reason: format!(\n                        \"failure count {} below threshold {}\",\n                        failure_count, self.config.force_failure_threshold\n                    ),\n                });\n            }\n        } else if self.config.first_failure_only && failure_count != 1 {\n            // Allow periodic retries after the first failure when configured,\n            // but never re-split a bead that is already a mitosis child.\n            let has_mitosis_depth_label =\n                bead.labels.iter().any(|l| l.starts_with(\"mitosis-depth:\"));\n            let is_repeat_tick = failure_count > 1\n                && self.config.repeat_interval > 0\n                && (failure_count - 1) % self.config.repeat_interval == 0\n                && !has_mitosis_depth_label;\n\n            if !is_repeat_tick {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    failure_count,\n                    first_failure_only = self.config.first_failure_only,\n                    repeat_interval = self.config.repeat_interval,\n                    \"mitosis skipped: not at trigger point\"\n                );\n                return Ok(MitosisResult::Skipped {\n                    reason: format!(\n                        \"not at trigger point (count={}, first_failure_only={}, repeat_interval={})\",\n                        failure_count, self.config.first_failure_only, self.config.repeat_interval\n                    ),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Resolve the agent adapter.\n        let adapter = match dispatcher.adapter(agent_name) {\n            Some(a) => a,\n            None => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    agent = agent_name,\n                    \"mitosis skipped: agent adapter not found\"\n                );\n                return Ok(MitosisResult::Skipped {\n                    reason: format!(\"adapter '{}' not found\", agent_name),\n                });\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Gather existing children for the prompt (so the agent avoids duplicates).\n        let existing_children = self.get_existing_children(store, &bead.id).await?;\n        let existing_children_text = if existing_children.is_empty() {\n            \"(no existing children)\".to_string()\n        } else {\n            existing_children\n                .iter()\n                .map(|t| format!(\"- {t}\"))\n                .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                .join(\"\\n\")\n        };\n\n        // Build mitosis prompt.\n        let prompt = prompt_builder\n            .build_mitosis(bead, workspace, \"mitosis\", &existing_children_text)\n            .context(\"failed to build mitosis prompt\")?;\n\n        // Acquire workspace flock for atomicity.\n        // The lock is automatically released when _lock goes out of scope.\n        // Note: Lock file persists but the file lock is released on drop.\n        let lock_path = self.lock_dir.join(format!(\n            \"needle-mitosis-{}.lock\",\n            sanitize_path_component(&workspace.display().to_string())\n        ));\n        let _lock = acquire_flock(&lock_path)\n            .await\n            .context(\"failed to acquire mitosis flock\")?;\n\n        tracing::info!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"dispatching agent for mitosis analysis\");\n\n        // Dispatch agent with mitosis prompt.\n        let exec_result = dispatcher\n            .dispatch(&bead.id, &prompt, adapter, workspace)\n            .await\n            .context(\"mitosis agent dispatch failed\")?;\n\n        // Parse the agent's response.\n        let response = parse_mitosis_response(&exec_result.stdout);\n\n        match response {\n            Some(resp) if resp.splittable && !resp.children.is_empty() => {\n                self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MitosisEvaluated {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    splittable: true,\n                    proposed_children: resp.children.len() as u32,\n                })?;\n\n                self.create_children(store, bead, &resp.children).await\n            }\n            Some(resp) if resp.splittable => {\n                // Splittable but no children proposed — treat as not splittable.\n                tracing::info!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"agent said splittable but proposed no children\"\n                );\n                self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MitosisEvaluated {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    splittable: false,\n                    proposed_children: 0,\n                })?;\n                Ok(MitosisResult::NotSplittable)\n            }\n            Some(resp) => {\n                // Log the reason if provided by the agent\n                if let Some(reason) = &resp.reason {\n                    tracing::info!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        reason = %reason,\n                        \"agent determined bead is single task (reason provided)\"\n                    );\n                } else {\n                    tracing::info!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"agent determined bead is single task\");\n                }\n                self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MitosisEvaluated {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    splittable: false,\n                    proposed_children: 0,\n                })?;\n                Ok(MitosisResult::NotSplittable)\n            }\n            None => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    exit_code = exec_result.exit_code,\n                    \"could not parse mitosis response from agent\"\n                );\n                self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MitosisEvaluated {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    splittable: false,\n                    proposed_children: 0,\n                })?;\n                Ok(MitosisResult::NotSplittable)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Evaluate a bead for timeout-triggered mitosis.\n    ///\n    /// This is a specialized analysis mode for beads that timed out after substantial\n    /// productive work. Unlike ordinary failure mitosis, this mode:\n    /// - Uses timeout context (elapsed duration, activity evidence)\n    /// - Distinguishes completed work from remaining work\n    /// - Proposes independently closable phases\n    /// - Refuses decomposition for hangs, infrastructure failures, or unsafe overlap\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `store` - Bead store for reading/writing beads\n    /// * `bead` - The bead that timed out\n    /// * `workspace` - Workspace directory\n    /// * `dispatcher` - Agent dispatcher\n    /// * `prompt_builder` - Prompt builder for templates\n    /// * `agent_name` - Name of the agent adapter to use\n    /// * `outcome` - Agent execution result (exit code, stdout, stderr)\n    /// * `duration` - Wall-clock duration of the agent execution\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    ///\n    /// * `Ok(MitosisResult)` - Outcome of the evaluation (Split, NotSplittable, Skipped, OutOfScope)\n    /// * `Err(e)` - Error during evaluation (non-fatal, bead is already released)\n    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\n    pub async fn evaluate_timeout(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        workspace: &Path,\n        dispatcher: &Dispatcher,\n        prompt_builder: &PromptBuilder,\n        agent_name: &str,\n        outcome: &AgentOutcome,\n        duration: Duration,\n    ) -> Result<MitosisResult> {\n        // Step 1: Check timeout eligibility (this is the gate for timeout-triggered mitosis)\n        let eligibility =\n            classify_timeout_eligibility(outcome, duration, &self.config.timeout_triggered);\n\n        // If not eligible, return early with a clear reason\n        if !eligibility.is_eligible() {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                reason = eligibility.reason(),\n                \"timeout does not qualify for mitosis\"\n            );\n            return Ok(MitosisResult::Skipped {\n                reason: eligibility.reason().to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            bead_id = %bead.id,\n            reason = eligibility.reason(),\n            \"timeout qualifies for mitosis analysis\"\n        );\n\n        // Step 2: Check if mitosis is enabled (general enablement)\n        if !self.config.enabled {\n            tracing::debug!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"mitosis disabled\");\n            return Ok(MitosisResult::Skipped {\n                reason: \"mitosis disabled\".to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Step 3: Check if bead references NEEDLE-internal configuration\n        if detects_needle_internal_config(bead) {\n            tracing::info!(\n                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                title = %bead.title,\n                \"timeout mitosis skipped: bead references NEEDLE-internal configuration\"\n            );\n            self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MitosisOutOfScope {\n                bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n            })?;\n            return Ok(MitosisResult::OutOfScope);\n        }\n\n        // Step 4: Check if the bead has exceeded the maximum mitosis depth\n        let current_depth = parse_mitosis_depth(bead);\n        if self.config.max_depth > 0 && current_depth >= self.config.max_depth {\n            tracing::info!(\n                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                current_depth,\n                max_depth = self.config.max_depth,\n                \"timeout mitosis skipped: bead has reached maximum generation depth\"\n            );\n            if let Err(e) = store.add_label(&bead.id, \"human\").await {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to add 'human' label to depth-limited bead\"\n                );\n            }\n            self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MitosisSkipped {\n                parent_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                existing_children: 0,\n            })?;\n            return Ok(MitosisResult::Skipped {\n                reason: format!(\n                    \"depth {} exceeds maximum depth {}\",\n                    current_depth, self.config.max_depth\n                ),\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Step 5: Resolve the agent adapter\n        let adapter = match dispatcher.adapter(agent_name) {\n            Some(a) => a,\n            None => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    agent = agent_name,\n                    \"timeout mitosis skipped: agent adapter not found\"\n                );\n                return Ok(MitosisResult::Skipped {\n                    reason: format!(\"adapter '{}' not found\", agent_name),\n                });\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Step 6: Gather existing children for deduplication\n        let existing_children = self.get_existing_children(store, &bead.id).await?;\n        let existing_children_text = if existing_children.is_empty() {\n            \"(no existing children)\".to_string()\n        } else {\n            existing_children\n                .iter()\n                .map(|t| format!(\"- {t}\"))\n                .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                .join(\"\\n\")\n        };\n\n        // Step 7: Build timeout-specific context for the prompt\n        let timeout_duration_secs = duration.as_secs();\n        let elapsed_duration = format_duration(duration);\n        let timeout_duration = format_timeout_duration(timeout_duration_secs);\n        let elapsed_percent = if timeout_duration_secs > 0 {\n            (duration.as_secs_f64() / timeout_duration_secs as f64 * 100.0).round()\n        } else {\n            0.0\n        };\n\n        // Build activity evidence description\n        let activity_evidence = build_activity_evidence_description(outcome);\n\n        let timeout_context = MitosisTimeoutContext {\n            elapsed_duration: &elapsed_duration,\n            timeout_duration: &timeout_duration,\n            elapsed_percent: &format!(\"{}%\", elapsed_percent),\n            activity_evidence: &activity_evidence,\n        };\n\n        // Step 8: Build timeout-specific mitosis prompt\n        let prompt = prompt_builder\n            .build_mitosis_timeout(\n                bead,\n                workspace,\n                \"mitosis-timeout\",\n                &existing_children_text,\n                &timeout_context,\n            )\n            .context(\"failed to build timeout mitosis prompt\")?;\n\n        // Step 9: Acquire workspace flock for atomicity.\n        // The lock is automatically released when _lock goes out of scope.\n        // Note: Lock file persists but the file lock is released on drop.\n        let lock_path = self.lock_dir.join(format!(\n            \"needle-mitosis-timeout-{}.lock\",\n            sanitize_path_component(&workspace.display().to_string())\n        ));\n        let _lock = acquire_flock(&lock_path)\n            .await\n            .context(\"failed to acquire timeout mitosis flock\")?;\n\n        tracing::info!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"dispatching agent for timeout mitosis analysis\");\n\n        // Step 10: Dispatch agent with timeout-specific prompt\n        let exec_result = dispatcher\n            .dispatch(&bead.id, &prompt, adapter, workspace)\n            .await\n            .context(\"timeout mitosis agent dispatch failed\")?;\n\n        // Step 11: Parse the agent's response\n        let response = parse_mitosis_response(&exec_result.stdout);\n\n        match response {\n            Some(resp) if resp.splittable && !resp.children.is_empty() => {\n                self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MitosisEvaluated {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    splittable: true,\n                    proposed_children: resp.children.len() as u32,\n                })?;\n\n                self.create_children(store, bead, &resp.children).await\n            }\n            Some(resp) if resp.splittable => {\n                // Splittable but no children proposed — treat as not splittable\n                tracing::info!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"agent said splittable but proposed no children for timeout\"\n                );\n                self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MitosisEvaluated {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    splittable: false,\n                    proposed_children: 0,\n                })?;\n                Ok(MitosisResult::NotSplittable)\n            }\n            Some(resp) => {\n                // Log the reason if provided by the agent (timeout-specific analysis)\n                if let Some(reason) = &resp.reason {\n                    tracing::info!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        reason = %reason,\n                        \"agent determined timeout bead is unsafe to split (reason provided)\"\n                    );\n                } else {\n                    tracing::info!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        \"agent determined timeout bead is single task or unsafe to split\"\n                    );\n                }\n                self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MitosisEvaluated {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    splittable: false,\n                    proposed_children: 0,\n                })?;\n                Ok(MitosisResult::NotSplittable)\n            }\n            None => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    exit_code = exec_result.exit_code,\n                    \"could not parse timeout mitosis response from agent\"\n                );\n                self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MitosisEvaluated {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    splittable: false,\n                    proposed_children: 0,\n                })?;\n                Ok(MitosisResult::NotSplittable)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create child beads with dedup against existing children.\n    async fn create_children(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        parent: &Bead,\n        proposed: &[ProposedChild],\n    ) -> Result<MitosisResult> {\n        // Enter the bead.mitosis span for the mitosis operation.\n        let mitosis_span = tracing::info_span!(\n            \"bead.mitosis\",\n            needle.bead.id = %parent.id,\n            needle.mitosis.proposed_children = proposed.len() as u32,\n            needle.mitosis.children_created = tracing::field::Empty, // Will be set based on result\n            needle.mitosis.children_skipped = tracing::field::Empty, // Will be set based on result\n        );\n\n        self.create_children_inner(store, parent, proposed)\n            .instrument(mitosis_span)\n            .await\n    }\n\n    async fn create_children_inner(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        parent: &Bead,\n        proposed: &[ProposedChild],\n    ) -> Result<MitosisResult> {\n        // Extract the root label from the parent for lineage tracking.\n        // If the parent has a root-* label, propagate it to children.\n        // Otherwise, this parent is the root of the lineage.\n        let root_label = extract_root_label(parent);\n\n        // Read parent's existing children AND all beads in the same lineage for comprehensive dedup.\n        // Lineage-wide dedup prevents duplicates across different generations in the same cascade.\n        let existing = self.get_existing_children(store, &parent.id).await?;\n        let lineage_beads = self.get_lineage_beads(store, &root_label).await?;\n\n        // Combine both sets: direct children + all lineage beads for dedup\n        let mut existing_titles: Vec<String> = existing.iter().map(|t| t.to_lowercase()).collect();\n        existing_titles.extend(lineage_beads.iter().map(|t| t.to_lowercase()));\n\n        // Deduplicate the titles list (in case a bead is both a direct child and in the lineage)\n        existing_titles.sort();\n        existing_titles.dedup();\n\n        // Compute the depth for child beads based on the parent's depth.\n        // If parent has no mitosis-depth label (depth 0), children get depth 1.\n        // If parent has mitosis-depth:N, children get depth N+1.\n        let parent_depth = parse_mitosis_depth(parent);\n        let child_depth = parent_depth + 1;\n\n        // Child beads carry parent-tracking labels for reliable dedup. Labels\n        // are stored on the bead itself and survive FrankenSQLite index\n        // corruption, unlike dependency relationships. All children in this\n        // split share the same label set.\n        let parent_label = format!(\"parent-{}\", parent.id);\n        let depth_label = format!(\"mitosis-depth:{}\", child_depth);\n        // HOOP Hook 4 (Stitch Label Inheritance): children of a mitosis split\n        // must keep the parent's stitch:* labels or they orphan from the\n        // Stitch that spawned the split.\n        let stitch_labels = crate::types::extract_stitch_prefixed_labels(&parent.labels);\n        let mut labels: Vec<&str> = vec![\"mitosis-child\", &depth_label, &parent_label, &root_label];\n        labels.extend(stitch_labels.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()));\n\n        // Dedup first, then build the list of children to create.\n        let mut to_create: Vec<NewChild> = Vec::new();\n        let mut skipped = 0u32;\n        for child in proposed {\n            // Dedup: does an existing child cover this task?\n            if existing_titles\n                .iter()\n                .any(|t| titles_match(t, &child.title.to_lowercase()))\n            {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    parent_id = %parent.id,\n                    child_title = %child.title,\n                    \"skipping duplicate child\"\n                );\n                skipped += 1;\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            to_create.push(NewChild {\n                title: &child.title,\n                body: &child.body,\n                labels: labels.as_slice(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Create all children and link each as a blocker of the parent in a\n        // single atomic operation. A crash mid-split (SIGKILL/OOM/eviction)\n        // rolls the whole thing back rather than leaving an orphaned child with\n        // no dependency link (plan.md Phase 5.3, Race 3). Backends without an\n        // atomic batch degrade to the historical sequential path.\n        let created_ids = if to_create.is_empty() {\n            Vec::new()\n        } else {\n            store\n                .split_bead(&parent.id, &to_create)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to split bead {}\", parent.id))?\n        };\n\n        for (child_id, child) in created_ids.iter().zip(to_create.iter()) {\n            tracing::info!(\n                parent_id = %parent.id,\n                child_id = %child_id,\n                child_title = %child.title,\n                \"created mitosis child\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        if created_ids.is_empty() {\n            // All proposed children already existed.\n            tracing::info!(\n                parent_id = %parent.id,\n                existing = existing.len(),\n                \"all proposed children already exist (dedup)\"\n            );\n            self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MitosisSkipped {\n                parent_id: parent.id.clone(),\n                existing_children: existing.len() as u32,\n            })?;\n            return Ok(MitosisResult::Skipped {\n                reason: \"all children already exist\".to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::MitosisSplit {\n            parent_id: parent.id.clone(),\n            children_created: created_ids.len() as u32,\n            children_skipped: skipped,\n            child_ids: created_ids.clone(),\n        })?;\n\n        // Record the final counts on the bead.mitosis span\n        tracing::Span::current()\n            .record(\"needle.mitosis.children_created\", created_ids.len() as u32);\n        tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.mitosis.children_skipped\", skipped);\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            parent_id = %parent.id,\n            children_created = created_ids.len(),\n            children_skipped = skipped,\n            \"mitosis split completed\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(MitosisResult::Split {\n            children: created_ids,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Read the failure count label from a bead.\n    ///\n    /// All br calls are wrapped in timeouts to prevent indefinite hang.\n    async fn get_failure_count(&self, store: &dyn BeadStore, bead_id: &BeadId) -> Result<u32> {\n        let labels =\n            match tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30), store.labels(bead_id))\n                .await\n            {\n                Ok(Ok(l)) => l,\n                Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead_id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to read labels for failure count\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(0);\n                }\n                Err(_) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead_id,\n                        \"labels() timed out after 30s, assuming failure count 0\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(0);\n                }\n            };\n\n        let count = labels\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|l| l.strip_prefix(\"failure-count:\"))\n            .filter_map(|n| n.parse::<u32>().ok())\n            .max()\n            .unwrap_or(0);\n\n        Ok(count)\n    }\n\n    /// Get titles of existing children for a parent bead.\n    ///\n    /// Uses label-based discovery (`parent-<parent_id>` label) instead of\n    /// reading the parent's dependency list. This is robust against\n    /// FrankenSQLite index corruption where `br dep add` creates the\n    /// dependency link and labels but the relationship doesn't appear in\n    /// `br show --json` output.\n    ///\n    /// The `list_all()` call is wrapped in a timeout to prevent indefinite\n    /// hang in HANDLING state.\n    async fn get_existing_children(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        parent_id: &BeadId,\n    ) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n        let parent_label = format!(\"parent-{}\", parent_id);\n        let all_beads = match tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n            store.list_all(),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(beads)) => beads,\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    parent_id = %parent_id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"list_all failed during get_existing_children, assuming no children\"\n                );\n                return Ok(Vec::new());\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    parent_id = %parent_id,\n                    \"list_all timed out after 30s during get_existing_children, assuming no children\"\n                );\n                return Ok(Vec::new());\n            }\n        };\n\n        let titles: Vec<String> = all_beads\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|b| b.labels.iter().any(|l| l == &parent_label))\n            .map(|b| b.title.clone())\n            .collect();\n\n        Ok(titles)\n    }\n\n    /// Get titles of all beads in the same lineage (sharing the same root label).\n    ///\n    /// This is used for lineage-wide deduplication during mitosis. In a multi-\n    /// generation cascade, we need to dedup against ALL beads created from the\n    /// same original root, not just direct children of the current parent.\n    ///\n    /// The `list_all()` call is wrapped in a timeout to prevent indefinite\n    /// hang in HANDLING state.\n    async fn get_lineage_beads(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        root_label: &str,\n    ) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n        let all_beads = match tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n            store.list_all(),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(beads)) => beads,\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    root_label,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"list_all failed during get_lineage_beads, assuming no lineage beads\"\n                );\n                return Ok(Vec::new());\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    root_label,\n                    \"list_all timed out after 30s during get_lineage_beads, assuming no lineage beads\"\n                );\n                return Ok(Vec::new());\n            }\n        };\n\n        let titles: Vec<String> = all_beads\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|b| b.labels.iter().any(|l| l == root_label))\n            .map(|b| b.title.clone())\n            .collect();\n\n        Ok(titles)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Parsing\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Parse the agent's mitosis analysis response from stdout.\n///\n/// Searches for a JSON object in the output. Handles markdown code fencing\n/// and surrounding text.\nfn parse_mitosis_response(stdout: &str) -> Option<MitosisResponse> {\n    // Try direct JSON parse first.\n    if let Ok(resp) = serde_json::from_str::<MitosisResponse>(stdout.trim()) {\n        return Some(resp);\n    }\n\n    // Try extracting JSON from markdown code fences.\n    let json_str = extract_json_block(stdout)?;\n    serde_json::from_str::<MitosisResponse>(json_str).ok()\n}\n\n/// Extract a JSON object from text that may contain markdown code fences.\nfn extract_json_block(text: &str) -> Option<&str> {\n    // Look for ```json ... ``` or ``` ... ``` blocks.\n    if let Some(start) = text.find(\"```json\") {\n        let content_start = start + \"```json\".len();\n        if let Some(end) = text[content_start..].find(\"```\") {\n            return Some(text[content_start..content_start + end].trim());\n        }\n    }\n\n    if let Some(start) = text.find(\"```\") {\n        let content_start = start + \"```\".len();\n        // Skip to next line if the opening ``` has text after it.\n        let content_start = text[content_start..]\n            .find('\\n')\n            .map(|n| content_start + n + 1)\n            .unwrap_or(content_start);\n        if let Some(end) = text[content_start..].find(\"```\") {\n            return Some(text[content_start..content_start + end].trim());\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Try to find a bare JSON object.\n    let trimmed = text.trim();\n    if trimmed.starts_with('{') {\n        // Find matching closing brace (simple heuristic).\n        let mut depth = 0i32;\n        for (i, ch) in trimmed.char_indices() {\n            match ch {\n                '{' => depth += 1,\n                '}' => {\n                    depth -= 1;\n                    if depth == 0 {\n                        return Some(&trimmed[..=i]);\n                    }\n                }\n                _ => {}\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    None\n}\n\n/// Sanitize a path string for use as a filename component.\nfn sanitize_path_component(s: &str) -> String {\n    s.chars()\n        .map(|c| {\n            if c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '-' || c == '_' {\n                c\n            } else {\n                '_'\n            }\n        })\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// Format a Duration into a human-readable string.\n///\n/// Examples: \"59m\", \"1h 30m\", \"45s\"\nfn format_duration(duration: Duration) -> String {\n    let secs = duration.as_secs();\n    if secs >= 3600 {\n        let hours = secs / 3600;\n        let minutes = (secs % 3600) / 60;\n        if minutes > 0 {\n            format!(\"{}h {}m\", hours, minutes)\n        } else {\n            format!(\"{}h\", hours)\n        }\n    } else if secs >= 60 {\n        let minutes = secs / 60;\n        let seconds = secs % 60;\n        if seconds > 0 {\n            format!(\"{}m {}s\", minutes, seconds)\n        } else {\n            format!(\"{}m\", minutes)\n        }\n    } else {\n        format!(\"{}s\", secs)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Format a timeout duration in seconds into a human-readable string.\n///\n/// Assumes timeout durations are typically in hours (e.g., 3600s -> \"1h\").\nfn format_timeout_duration(secs: u64) -> String {\n    format_duration(Duration::from_secs(secs))\n}\n\n/// Build a description of activity evidence from an agent outcome.\n///\n/// This describes what the agent was doing when it timed out, helping the\n/// mitosis analysis distinguish between productive work and infrastructure hangs.\nfn build_activity_evidence_description(outcome: &AgentOutcome) -> String {\n    let mut evidence = Vec::new();\n\n    // Check stdout for structured output\n    if !outcome.stdout.is_empty() {\n        evidence.push(\"Agent produced structured output before timeout\".to_string());\n    }\n\n    // Check stderr for tool-use calls\n    if !outcome.stderr.is_empty() {\n        let stderr_lower = outcome.stderr.to_lowercase();\n        let tool_markers = [\n            \"tool_use:\",\n            \"tool_use_id\",\n            \"useagent\",\n            \"useread\",\n            \"usebash\",\n            \"uselsp\",\n            \"useedit\",\n            \"usewrite\",\n            \"<invoke>\",\n            \"tool_result\",\n        ];\n\n        for marker in &tool_markers {\n            if stderr_lower.contains(marker) {\n                evidence.push(\"Agent emitted tool-use calls (active work)\".to_string());\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // If no evidence found\n    if evidence.is_empty() {\n        evidence.push(\"No clear activity evidence (empty stdout/stderr)\".to_string());\n    }\n\n    evidence.join(\"; \")\n}\n\n/// Check if two titles match (fuzzy comparison for dedup).\n///\n/// Considers titles matching if they are identical after normalization,\n/// or if one contains the other as a substring.\n/// Falls back to token-set Jaccard similarity after stripping stopwords\n/// to catch semantically identical titles with different phrasing.\nfn titles_match(existing: &str, proposed: &str) -> bool {\n    if existing == proposed {\n        return true;\n    }\n\n    // Normalize: remove common prefixes and compare.\n    let normalize = |s: &str| -> String {\n        s.trim()\n            .trim_start_matches(|c: char| !c.is_alphabetic())\n            .to_lowercase()\n    };\n\n    let e = normalize(existing);\n    let p = normalize(proposed);\n\n    // Fast path: exact match or substring match\n    if e == p || e.contains(&p) || p.contains(&e) {\n        return true;\n    }\n\n    // Fallback: fuzzy similarity using token-set Jaccard similarity\n    // Strip stopwords and common verbs first, then compare token sets\n    let stopwords = [\n        // Common verification verbs (semantically equivalent in this context)\n        \"verify\",\n        \"confirm\",\n        \"validate\",\n        \"check\",\n        \"ensure\",\n        \"test\",\n        \"assert\",\n        \"inspect\",\n        // Articles and conjunctions\n        \"the\",\n        \"a\",\n        \"an\",\n        \"and\",\n        \"or\",\n        \"but\",\n        // Prepositions\n        \"for\",\n        \"to\",\n        \"in\",\n        \"on\",\n        \"at\",\n        \"by\",\n        \"with\",\n        \"from\",\n        \"of\",\n        \"about\",\n        // Pronouns and demonstratives\n        \"that\",\n        \"this\",\n        \"these\",\n        \"those\",\n        \"it\",\n        \"its\",\n        // Common task words\n        \"uses\",\n        \"use\",\n        \"used\",\n        \"not\",\n        \"no\",\n        \"should\",\n        \"will\",\n        \"can\",\n        \"may\",\n        // Data access verbs (often interchangeable)\n        \"get\",\n        \"fetch\",\n        \"retrieve\",\n        \"read\",\n        \"reads\",\n        \"load\",\n        \"pull\",\n        // Action verbs (often interchangeable)\n        \"add\",\n        \"create\",\n        \"make\",\n        \"build\",\n        \"implement\",\n        \"update\",\n        \"change\",\n        \"modify\",\n        \"adjust\",\n        \"fix\",\n        \"remove\",\n        \"delete\",\n        \"clear\",\n        \"set\",\n        \"configure\",\n        \"adjust\",\n        // Adjectives (often interchangeable in task titles)\n        \"correctly\",\n        \"correct\",\n        \"properly\",\n        \"proper\",\n        \"accurately\",\n        \"accurate\",\n    ];\n\n    // Token normalization map for abbreviations and common synonyms\n    let normalize_token = |word: &str| -> String {\n        match word.to_lowercase().as_str() {\n            // Percentage abbreviations\n            \"pct\" | \"pct.\" | \"percent\" | \"perc\" => \"percentage\".to_string(),\n            // Model-related terms\n            \"agnostic\" => \"model\".to_string(), // \"model-agnostic\" ~ \"rotated model\"\n            \"rotated\" => \"scoped\".to_string(), // \"rotated model\" = \"scoped model\" in NEEDLE context\n            // Calculation-related\n            \"calc\" => \"calculation\".to_string(),\n            \"feeds\" | \"feed\" => \"uses\".to_string(), // \"feeds EMA\" ~ \"uses\"\n            w => w.to_lowercase(),\n        }\n    };\n\n    let tokenize = |s: &str| -> std::collections::HashSet<String> {\n        s.split_whitespace()\n            .flat_map(|word| {\n                // Split on hyphens and underscores to handle compound words\n                // e.g., \"model-agnostic\" -> [\"model\", \"agnostic\"]\n                word.split(['-', '_'])\n                    .map(normalize_token)\n                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            })\n            .filter(|word| !stopwords.contains(&word.as_str()))\n            .filter(|word| word.len() > 1) // Skip single-character words\n            .collect()\n    };\n\n    let e_tokens = tokenize(&e);\n    let p_tokens = tokenize(&p);\n\n    // Calculate Jaccard similarity: |intersection| / |union|\n    let intersection = e_tokens.intersection(&p_tokens).count();\n    let union = e_tokens.union(&p_tokens).count();\n\n    if union == 0 {\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    let jaccard = intersection as f64 / union as f64;\n\n    // Threshold 0.6: requires 60% token overlap\n    // High enough to avoid false positives, low enough to catch semantic duplicates\n    jaccard >= 0.6\n}\n\n/// Parse the mitosis depth from a bead's labels.\n///\n/// Returns the depth value if a mitosis-depth label exists and is valid,\n/// otherwise returns 0 (indicating this is not a mitosis child).\nfn parse_mitosis_depth(bead: &Bead) -> u32 {\n    bead.labels\n        .iter()\n        .filter_map(|l| l.strip_prefix(\"mitosis-depth:\"))\n        .filter_map(|n| n.parse::<u32>().ok())\n        .max()\n        .unwrap_or(0)\n}\n\n/// Extract the root label from a bead for lineage tracking.\n///\n/// If the bead has a root-* label, returns it (propagating the existing lineage root).\n/// Otherwise, this bead is the root of its lineage, so we return root-<bead_id>.\nfn extract_root_label(bead: &Bead) -> String {\n    bead.labels\n        .iter()\n        .find(|l| l.starts_with(\"root-\"))\n        .cloned()\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| format!(\"root-{}\", bead.id))\n}\n\n/// Detect if a bead references NEEDLE-internal configuration.\n///\n/// Returns true if the bead content suggests investigating or fixing NEEDLE's own\n/// dispatch configuration (Pluck, exclude_labels, bead discovery, etc.).\n/// These tasks have no legitimate resolution path from inside a target repo.\npub fn detects_needle_internal_config(bead: &Bead) -> bool {\n    let combined_text = format!(\n        \"{} {}\",\n        bead.title.to_lowercase(),\n        bead.body\n            .as_ref()\n            .map(|b| b.to_lowercase())\n            .unwrap_or_default()\n    );\n\n    // Patterns that indicate NEEDLE-internal configuration work.\n    // These are derived from the real ARMOR incident (bead bf-3b64 and its lineage).\n    let internal_config_patterns = [\n        \"pluck configuration\",\n        \"pluck config\",\n        \"exclude_labels\",\n        \"exclude labels\",\n        \"bead discovery\",\n        \"starvation alert\",\n        \"beads invisible to worker\",\n        \"open beads exist but pluck found none\",\n        \"needle dispatch\",\n        \"strand configuration\",\n        \"worker configuration\",\n        \"bead filtering\",\n        \"candidate exclusion\",\n    ];\n\n    for pattern in &internal_config_patterns {\n        if combined_text.contains(pattern) {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                pattern,\n                \"bead references NEEDLE-internal configuration\"\n            );\n            return true;\n        }\n    }\n\n    false\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// \"c\"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();\n        let set2: HashSet<String> = [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();\n\n        // Identical sets should have Jaccard similarity of 1.0\n        assert_eq!(jaccard_similarity(&set1, &set2), 1.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn jaccard_both_empty() {\n        let set1: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();\n        let set2: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();\n\n        // Two empty sets are defined as identical\n        assert_eq!(jaccard_similarity(&set1, &set2), 1.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn jaccard_one_empty() {\n        let set1: HashSet<String> = [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();\n        let set2: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();\n\n        // One empty, one non-empty should have 0.0 similarity\n        assert_eq!(jaccard_similarity(&set1, &set2), 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn jaccard_no_overlap() {\n        let set1: HashSet<String> = [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();\n        let set2: HashSet<String> = [\"x\", \"y\", \"z\"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();\n\n        // No overlap should have 0.0 similarity\n        assert_eq!(jaccard_similarity(&set1, &set2), 0.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn jaccard_partial_overlap() {\n        let set1: HashSet<String> = [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();\n        let set2: HashSet<String> = [\"a\", \"b\", \"d\"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();\n\n        // Intersection: {a, b} (2 elements)\n        // Union: {a, b, c, d} (4 elements)\n        // Jaccard: 2/4 = 0.5\n        assert_eq!(jaccard_similarity(&set1, &set2), 0.5);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn jaccard_subset() {\n        let set1: HashSet<String> = [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();\n        let set2: HashSet<String> = [\"a\", \"b\"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();\n\n        // set2 is a subset of set1\n        // Intersection: {a, b} (2 elements)\n        // Union: {a, b, c} (3 elements)\n        // Jaccard: 2/3 ≈ 0.6667\n        let result = jaccard_similarity(&set1, &set2);\n        assert!((result - 0.6667).abs() < 0.0001);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn jaccard_high_overlap() {\n        let set1: HashSet<String> = [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\", \"d\", \"e\"]\n            .iter()\n            .map(|s| s.to_string())\n            .collect();\n        let set2: HashSet<String> = [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\", \"d\", \"f\"]\n            .iter()\n            .map(|s| s.to_string())\n            .collect();\n\n        // Intersection: {a, b, c, d} (4 elements)\n        // Union: {a, b, c, d, e, f} (6 elements)\n        // Jaccard: 4/6 ≈ 0.6667\n        let result = jaccard_similarity(&set1, &set2);\n        assert!((result - 0.6667).abs() < 0.0001);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn jaccard_completely_different_sizes() {\n        let set1: HashSet<String> = [\"a\"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();\n        let set2: HashSet<String> = [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\", \"d\", \"e\", \"f\", \"g\", \"h\", \"i\", \"j\"]\n            .iter()\n            .map(|s| s.to_string())\n            .collect();\n\n        // Intersection: {a} (1 element)\n        // Union: {a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j} (10 elements)\n        // Jaccard: 1/10 = 0.1\n        assert_eq!(jaccard_similarity(&set1, &set2), 0.1);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn jaccard_symmetric() {\n        let set1: HashSet<String> = [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();\n        let set2: HashSet<String> = [\"a\", \"b\", \"d\"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();\n\n        // Jaccard similarity should be symmetric\n        assert_eq!(\n            jaccard_similarity(&set1, &set2),\n            jaccard_similarity(&set2, &set1)\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn jaccard_single_element_match() {\n        let set1: HashSet<String> = [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();\n        let set2: HashSet<String> = [\"a\"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();\n\n        // Intersection: {a} (1 element)\n        // Union: {a, b, c} (3 elements)\n        // Jaccard: 1/3 ≈ 0.3333\n        let result = jaccard_similarity(&set1, &set2);\n        assert!((result - 0.3333).abs() < 0.0001);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn jaccard_integration_with_token_set() {\n        // Test integration with token_set_without_stopwords\n        let title1 = \"verify API endpoint authentication\";\n        let When the home workspace has no work (Pluck returned NoWork) and\n//! maintenance is clean (Mend returned NoWork), Explore searches\n//! configured workspaces for claimable beads.\n//!\n//! ## Workspace Discovery (Intended Default)\n//!\n//! **DEFAULT MODE (RECOMMENDED):** Empty `workspaces` config.\n//!\n//! When `config.workspaces` is empty (the default), Explore runs recursive\n//! workspace discovery under `config.workspace_root`. All directories containing\n//! a `.beads/` subdirectory are automatically scanned for beads.\n//!\n//! This is the **intended default for the fleet as a whole** — new workspaces\n//! are picked up automatically without configuration changes. Operators should\n//! leave `workspaces` empty unless there's a specific reason to pin a worker to\n//! a fixed repo set.\n//!\n//! **PINNED MODE (EXCEPTION):** Explicit `workspaces` list.\n//!\n//! When `config.workspaces` is non-empty, auto-discovery is disabled and only\n//! the specified paths are scanned. Use this to restrict a specific worker to\n//! a fixed repo set (e.g., a dedicated worker for a high-priority workspace).\n//!\n//! This is an **exception mechanism**. The fleet should normally run with\n//! `workspaces` empty. A WARN log is emitted at startup when `workspaces` is\n//! non-empty, naming the pinned repos, so operators can immediately see when\n//! a worker is running in restricted mode.\n//!\n//! ## Design Constraints (from v1 lessons)\n//! - **No upward traversal.** Only configured paths are checked.\n//! - **Static workspace list.** Read from config at boot, not re-evaluated.\n//! - **No permanent relocation.** Workers process one bead then return home.\n//!\n//! ## Implementation\n//!\n//!         max_interval_cycles,\n            consecutive_empty_scans: 0,\n            cycles_until_scan: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Return the effective interval after the recorded empty scans.\n    fn effective_interval_cycles(&self) -> u32 {\n        let multiplier = 1u32\n            .checked_shl(self.consecutive_empty_scans.min(31))\n            .unwrap_or(u32::MAX);\n        self.base_interval_cycles\n            .saturating_mul(multiplier)\n            .min(self.max_interval_cycles)\n    }\n\n    /// Decide whether this selection cycle should perform an Explore scan.\n    fn should_scan(&mut self) -> bool {\n        if self.cycles_until_scan == 0 {\n            true\n        } else {\n            self.cycles_until_scan -= 1;\n            false\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record the outcome of a real scan and schedule the next one.\n    fn record_scan(&mut self, found_candidate: bool) {\n        if found_candidate {\n            self.consecutive_empty_scans = 0;\n            self.cycles_until_scan = self.base_interval_cycles.saturating_sub(1);\n            return;\n        }\n\n        self.consecutive_empty_scans = self.consecutive_empty_scans.saturating_add(1);\n        self.cycles_until_scan = self.effective_interval_cycles().saturating_sub(1);\n    }\n}\n\n/// The Explore strand — discovers beads in other      worker = %qualified_id,\n                configured_rediscovery_cycles = config.rediscovery_cycles,\n                \"Explore auto-discovery: workspaces re-discovered every cycle \\\n                 (rediscovery_cycles throttle no longer applied)\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        ExploreStrand {\n            enabled: config.enabled,\n            workspaces: std::sync::Mutex::new(workspaces),\n            home_workspace,\n            registry,\n            telemetry,\n            qualified_id,\n            store_factory: Arc::new(DefaultStoreFactory),\n            cycles_since_rediscovery: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32::new(0),\n            rediscovery_cycles: config.rediscovery_cycles,\n            workspace_root: config.workspace_root,\n            auto_discovery_mode,\n            starvation_threshold_minutes: config.starvation_threshold_minutes,\n            last_successful_claim_seconds: AtomicU64::new(0),\n            ready_beads_detected: AtomicU64::new(0),\n            last_scan_per_workspace: std::sync::Mutex::new(std::collections::HashMap::new()),\n            scan_backoff: std::sync::Mutex::new(ExploreScanBackoff::new(\n                config.scan_interval_cycles,\n                config.max_scan_interval_cycles,\n            )),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new ExploreStrand for testing with explicit workspace list.\n Return whether this cycle should perform the remote workspace scan.\n    fn should_scan_this_cycle(&self) -> bool {\n        self.scan_backoff.lock().unwrap().should_scan()\n    }\n\n    /// Record a completed Explore scan and update its future cadence.\n    fn record_scan_result(&self, found_candidate: bool) {\n        let mut backoff = self.scan_backoff.lock().unwrap();\n        backoff.record_scan(found_candidate);\n        tracing::debug!(\n            worker = %self.qualified_id,\n            found_candidate,\n            consecutive_empty_scans = Discover all workspaces under a root path.\n    ///\n    /// A workspace is any directory containing a `.beads/` subdirectory.\n    /// Returns an empty vector if the root doesn't exist or cannot be read.\n    fn discover_workspaces(root: &Path) -> Vec<PathBuf> {\n        let mut discovered = Vec::new();\n\n        // If root doesn't exist, return empty (not an error).\n        if !root.exists() {\n            tracing::debug!(root = %root.display(), \"workspace root does not exist, no workspaces discovered\");\n            return discovered;\n        }\n\n        // Read the directory; non-existent or unreadable dirs return empty.\n        let entries = match fs::read_dir(root) {\n            Ok(entries) => entries,\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::debug!(root = %root.display(), error = %e, \"failed to read workspace root\");\n                return discovered;\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Filter for entries containing a `.beads/` subdirectory.\n        for entry in entries {\n            let entry = match entry {\n                Ok(e) => e,\n                Err(_) => continue,\n            };\n\n            let path = entry.path();\n            if path.is_dir() && Self::has_beads_dir(&path) {\n                tracing::debug!(workspace = %path.display(), \"discovered workspace\");\n                discovered.push(path);\n            }\n        }\n\n        tracing::debug!(\n            root = %root.display(),\n            count = discovered.len(),\n            \"workspace discovery complete\"\n        );\n\n        discovered\n    }\n\n    /// Check if a workspace path has a `.beads/` directory.\n    fn has_beads_dir(workspace: &Path) -> bool {\n        workspace.join(\".beads\").is_dir()\n    }\n\n    /// Re-discover workspaces (refresh the workspace list).\n    ///\n    /// This is called periodically when `rediscovery_cycles` > 0 and we're in\n    /// auto-discovery mode (empty workspaces config). It re-runs discovery under\n    /// `workspace_root` and updates the workspace list, preserving:\n    /// - **No upward traversal:** Only scans immediate children of workspace_root\n    /// - **Explicit workspaces override:** Only runs when auto_discovery_mode is true\n    ///\n    /// Returns the number of new workspaces discovered (if any).\n    fn rediscover_workspaces(&self) -> usize {\n        // Skip re-discovery if we're in pinned mode (explicit workspaces list).\n        if !self.auto_discovery_mode {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                worker = %self.qualified_id,\n                \"skipping workspace re-discovery: running in pinned mode (explicit workspaces list)\"\n            );\n            return 0;\n        }\n\n        // NOTE: re-discovery is now run every cycle (bf-6anj4). The historical\n        // `rediscovery_cycles == 0` disable path was removed; the only skip that\n        // remains is pinned mode (handled above).\n        let previous_count = {\n            let workspaces = self.workspaces.lock().unwrap();\n            workspaces.len()\n        };\n\n        let new_workspaces = Self::discover_workspaces(&self.workspace_root);\n        let new_count = new_workspaces.len();\n\n        // Update the workspace list.\n        {\n            let mut workspaces = self.workspaces.lock().unwrap();\n            *workspaces = new_workspaces;\n        }\n\n        let added_count = new_count.saturating_sub(previous_count);\n\n        if added_count > 0 {\n            tracing::info!(\n                worker = %self.qualified_id,\n                previous_count,\n                new_count,\n                added_count,\n                \"workspace re-discovery found new workspaces\"\n            );\n        } else {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                worker = %self.qualified_id,\n                previous_count,\n                \"workspace re-discovery: no change (still {} workspaces)\",\n                previous_count\n            );\n        }\n\n        added_count\n    }\n\n    /// Compute the starting workspace index for this worker.\n    ///\n    /// Uses a hash of the qualified_id modulo the workspace count to determine\n    /// where this worker should start scanning. This de-herds workers by ensuring\n    /// they start at different positions in the workspace list.\n    ///\n    /// Returns 0 if there are no workspaces (defensive, should be handled earlier).\n    ///\n    /// Superseded in production by the per-cycle shuffle in `evaluate()` (bf-6anj4);\n    /// retained (and exercised by unit tests) as documentation of the prior\n    /// static-rotation de-herd model.\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    fn compute_start_index(&self) -> usize {\n        let workspaces = self.workspaces.lock().unwrap();\n        if workspaces.is_empty() {\n            return 0;\n        }\n\n        let n = workspaces.len();\n\n        // Hash the qualified_id using a stable hash algorithm\n        let mut hasher = DefaultHasher::new();\n        self.qualified_id.hash(&mut hasher);\n        let hash = hasher.finish();\n\n        // Start at hash % n, wrapping around\n        (hash as usize) % n\n    }\n\n    /// Get an iterator over workspaces in this worker's rotation order.\n    ///\n    /// The iterator starts at this worker's computed start index and wraps around,\n    /// covering all workspaces exactly once. Each worker with a different qualified_id\n    /// will visit workspaces in a different rotation.\n    ///\n    /// Superseded in production by the per-cycle shuffle in `evaluate()` (bf-6anj4);\n    /// retained (and exercised by unit tests) as documentation of the prior model.\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    fn rotated_workspace_order(&self) -> Vec<PathBuf> {\n        // Compute the start index *before* taking the lock below:\n        // `compute_start_index()` acquires `self.workspaces` itself, and\n        // `std::sync::Mutex` is not reentrant — calling it while already\n        // holding the lock here previously self-deadlocked every time this\n        // function ran (see bf-2unnq).\n        let start = self.compute_start_index();\n\n        let workspaces = self.workspaces.lock().unwrap();\n        if workspaces.is_empty() {\n            return vec![];\n        }\n\n        let n = workspaces.len();\n        // Defensive: `compute_start_index()` released its lock before we\n        // re-acquired ours above, so guard against the (currently\n        // never-concurrent, but cheap to guard) case where the count\n        // changed in between.\n        let start = start % n;\n        let mut rotated = Vec::with_capacity(n);\n\n        // Add workspaces from start to end\n        for i in start..n {\n            rotated.push(workspaces[i].clone());\n        }\n\n        // Add workspaces from beginning to start (wrap-around)\n        for i in 0..start {\n            rotated.push(workspaces[i].clone());\n        }\n\n        rotated\n    }\n\n    /// Create a bead store for a workspace's explicit backend binding.\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    async fn store_for_workspace(workspace: &Path) -> Result<Arc<dyn BeadStore>, anyhow::Error> {\n        discover_default(\n            workspace.to_path_buf(),\n            None,\n            Some(\"needle\".to_string()),\n            Some(env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\").to_string()),\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Create the descriptor-bound store for a workspace path.\n    ///\n    /// This internal version is marked pub(crate) to allow testing with store injection.\n    #[cfg(test)]\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    async fn create_store_for(\n        &self,\n        workspace: &Path,\n    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn BeadStore>, anyhow::Error> {\n        self.store_factory.create_store(workspace).await\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait::async_trait]\nimpl super::Strand for ExploreStrand {\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        \"explore\"\n    }\n\n    async fn evaluate(\n        &self,\n        _store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        _exclusions: &HashSet<BeadId>,\n    ) -> StrandResult {\n        use std::time::Instant;\n\n        // If disabled, nothing to explore.\n        if !self.enabled {\n            let _ = self\n                .telemetry\n                .emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::StrandSkipped {\n                    strand_name: \"explore\".to_string(),\n                    reason: \"disabled\".to_string(),\n                });\n            return StrandResult::NoWork;\n        }\n\n        // A backoff skip is still reported as NoWork so the waterfall continues\n        // evaluating Weave and all later escalation strands in their normal\n        // order; only Explore's remote scan is deferred.\n        if !self.should_scan_this_cycle() {\n            let _ = self\n                .telemetry\n                .emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::StrandSkipped {\n                    strand_name: \"explore\".to_string(),\n                    reason: \"adaptive_scan_backoff\".to_string(),\n                });\n            tracing::debug!(\n                worker = %self.qualified_id,\n                \"Explore scan deferred by adaptive empty-scan backoff\"\n            );\n            return StrandResult::NoWork;\n        }\n\n        // Re-discover workspaces every cycle (bf-3peh4 / bf-6anj4). The workspace\n        // list was captured at boot and only refreshed on a throttle, so a newly\n        // created store needed a worker restart to be seen. A plain read_dir over\n        // ~40 entries is cheap, so we refresh unconditionally each cycle;\n        // `rediscover_workspaces` is a no-op in pinned mode. The cycle counter is\n        // still advanced so telemetry/consumers that read it stay meaningful.\n        let _cycle = self\n            .cycles_since_rediscovery\n            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed)\n            + 1;\n        let added = self.rediscover_workspaces();\n        if added > 0 {\n            tracing::info!(\n                worker = %self.qualified_id,\n                added,\n                \"workspace re-discovery found new workspaces\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Empty workspaces (after discovery attempt) means no workspaces found.\n        {\n            let workspaces = self.workspaces.lock().unwrap();\n            if workspaces.is_empty() {\n                let _ = self\n                    .telemetry\n                    .emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::StrandSkipped {\n                        strand_name: \"explore\".to_string(),\n                        reason: \"no_workspaces_discovered\".to_string(),\n                    });\n                self.record_scan_result(false);\n                return StrandResult::NoWork;\n            }\n        }\n\n        let filters = Filters {\n            assignee: None,\n            exclude_labels: vec![\n                \"deferred\".to_string(),\n                \"human\".to_string(),\n                \"blocked\".to_string(),\n            ],\n            exclude_ids: HashSet::new(),\n        };\n\n        // Shuffle this worker's workspace scan order fresh every cycle (bf-6anj4).\n        // The previous static `compute_start_index` (hash(qualified_id) % N) was\n        // constant for a worker's whole session, so a worker whose fixed index\n        // landed near an always-non-empty (or always-excluded) workspace could\n        // permanently starve later workspaces. A fresh shuffle each cycle de-herds\n        // workers without pinning coverage to a static, identity-derived value.\n        let mut workspaces = {\n            let workspaces = self.workspaces.lock().unwrap();\n            workspaces.clone()\n        };\n        {\n            use rand::seq::SliceRandom;\n            workspaces.shuffle(&mut rand::thread_rng());\n        }\n        let total_workspaces = workspaces.len();\n\n        tracing::debug!(\n            qualified_id = %self.qualified_id,\n            total_workspaces,\n            \"worker scan: shuffled order over {} workspaces this cycle\",\n            total_workspaces\n        );\n\n        // Track scan summary information for telemetry\n        let scan_start = Instant::now();\n        let mut workspaces_visited: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n        let mut workspaces_with_candidates: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n        let mut total_candidates = 0usize;\n        let mut exclusion_reasons: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();\n\n        // Aggregate candidates across ALL workspaces rather than returning on the\n        // first non-empty one (bf-4df1e / bf-47bfm). Previously a single stale or\n        // excluded bead in an early workspace caused an early return; the outer\n        // waterfall then filtered it out and fell through to the next strand,\n        // never scanning the remaining workspaces — silently starving the fleet.\n        // We now scan every workspace, collect all candidates, and rank them\n        // globally before returning.\n        let mut all_candidates: Vec<crate::types::Bead> = Vec::new();\n\n        for workspace in &workspaces {\n            // Track this workspace as visited\n            let workspace_str = workspace.display().to_string();\n            workspaces_visited.push(workspace_str.clone());\n\n            // Skip the home workspace — Pluck already checked it.\n            if workspace == &self.home_workspace {\n                tracing::debug!(workspace = %workspace.display(), \"skipping home workspace\");\n                exclusion_reasons.insert(\"home_workspace\".to_string());\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Check that .beads/ exists before attempting to query.\n            if !Self::has_beads_dir(workspace) {\n                tracing::debug!(workspace = %workspace.display(), \"no .beads/ directory, skipping\");\n                exclusion_reasons.insert(\"no_beads_dir\".to_string());\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Create a store for this workspace and query for ready beads.\n            let remote_store = match self.store_factory.create_store(workspace).await {\n                Ok(s) => s,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        workspace = %workspace.display(),\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to create bead store for workspace, skipping\"\n                    );\n                    exclusion_reasons.insert(format!(\"store_error: {}\", e));\n                    continue;\n                }\n            };\n\n            match remote_store.ready(&filters).await {\n                Ok(mut candidates) => {\n                    // Defensive belt-and-suspenders filtering.\n                    // The store.ready() method receives exclude_labels in its Filters,\n                    // but some backend implementations may not filter correctly.\n                    // This ensures excluded/assigned beads are never returned as candidates.\n                    let before_count = candidates.len();\n                    candidates.retain(|b| {\n                        let assignee_ok = b.assignee.is_none();\n                        let labels_ok =\n                            !b.labels.iter().any(|l| filters.exclude_labels.contains(l));\n                        assignee_ok && labels_ok\n                    });\n                    let filtered_count = before_count - candidates.len();\n\n                    if filtered_count > 0 {\n                        exclusion_reasons.insert(format!(\"filtered_{}\", filtered_count));\n                    }\n\n                    if candidates.is_empty() {\n                        // No ready candidates. Run cross-workspace mend to release\n                        // orphaned in-progress beads, then re-query.\n                        tracing::debug!(\n                            workspace = %workspace.display(),\n                            \"no ready candidates, running cross-workspace mend\"\n                        );\n                        exclusion_reasons.insert(\"no_ready_candidates\".to_string());\n\n                        // Only run cleanup if there are actually in-progress beads.\n                        // This avoids unnecessary spawn_blocking calls that can deadlock\n                        // in test environments with limited blocking thread pools.\n                        let all_beads = match remote_store.list_all().await {\n                            Ok(beads) => beads,\n                            Err(e) => {\n                                tracing::warn!(\n                                    workspace = %workspace.display(),\n                                    error = %e,\n                                    \"failed to list beads for orphan check, skipping\"\n                                );\n                                exclusion_reasons.insert(format!(\"list_error: {}\", e));\n                                continue;\n                            }\n                        };\n\n                        let has_in_progress = all_beads\n                            .iter()\n                            .any(|b| b.status == crate::types::BeadStatus::InProgress);\n\n continue;\n                        }\n\n                        match super::cleanup_orphaned_in_progress(\n                            remote_store.as_ref(),\n                            &self.registry,\n                            &self.telemetry,\n                            &self.qualified_id,\n                        )\n                        .await\n                        {\n                            Ok(released) if released > 0 => {\n                                tracing::info!(\n                                    workspace = %workspace.display(),\n                                    released,\n                                    \"cross-workspace mend released orphans, re-querying\"\n                                );\n\n                                // Re-query
